caption_en:
The crew that refused to leave is the part nobody remembers. ✈️

27 Jun 1976: Air France flight 139, Tel Aviv to Paris, is hijacked after a stop in Athens by members of the PFLP (Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine) and German radicals, and flown to Entebbe, Uganda.
The hijackers separate the Israeli and Jewish passengers; the others are set free (Britannica). Captain Michel Bacos is told he can leave. He refuses: "I told my crew that we must stay until the end." His whole crew stays (NPR, 2019).
3 to 4 Jul 1976: four Israeli Hercules planes fly about 4,000 km. Within an hour of landing the hostages are free; over 100 come home (Britannica).

Three hostages were killed, and so was the commander, Yoni Netanyahu.

Would your country fly 4,000 km for you? Tell me below.

Sources: Britannica, Entebbe raid; NPR (2019).
Photos (Wikimedia Commons): US Army (public domain); Oren Rozen (CC BY-SA 4.0); Micha Sender (CC BY-SA 3.0); Moshe Milner, GPO (CC BY-SA 3.0); Israel Preker, PikiWiki (CC BY 2.5). Map: Natural Earth. AI voice.
caption_he:
4,000 ק"מ. פחות משעה על הקרקע.
27 ביוני 1976: טיסת אייר פראנס 139 מתל אביב לפריז נחטפת אחרי עצירה באתונה, ומוטסת לאנטבה שבאוגנדה.
החוטפים מפרידים את הישראלים והיהודים, ומשחררים את השאר. הקברניט הצרפתי מישל בקוס מסרב לעזוב, וכל הצוות נשאר איתו.
ב 3 ביולי ארבעה מטוסי הרקולס טסים כ 4,000 ק"מ. תוך שעה מהנחיתה בני הערובה חופשיים, ויותר מ 100 חוזרים הביתה.
שלושה בני ערובה נהרגו, וגם המפקד, יוני נתניהו.
המדינה שלכם הייתה טסה 4,000 ק"מ בשבילכם? כתבו לי.

lines.line: Four thousand kilometres. Under one hour on the ground.
June 27, 1976. Air France flight 139, from Tel Aviv to Paris, is hijacked after a stop in Athens.
The hijackers, from the PFLP, the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, and German radicals, fly it to Entebbe, Uganda.
There they split the passengers. Israelis and Jews on one side. The others are set free.
The French captain, Michel Bacos, is told he can go. He refuses. His whole crew stays.
July 3. Four Israeli Hercules planes fly four thousand kilometres south.
They land at night. Within an hour, the hostages are free.
Over a hundred hostages, flown home.
Three hostages were killed. So was the commander, Yoni Netanyahu.
Would your country fly four thousand kilometres for you? Tell me below.
Because that's how far they flew.
